questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. It is unquestionably evident that this virus brought misery and grief into the lives of people of other professions too.

B. Covid-19 changed the form and face of every field in the world. It did not leave any field untouched.

C. One of the most affected areas is education. Millions of students all over the world could not get a proper education.

D. Millions of teachers who are working, specifically in private educational institutes, were not paid a full salary during the pandemic.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "BCDA"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• Let's look at the correct sequence of the passage. 
 
• Statement B is the opening sentence of the passage which explains that every field in the world has transformed because to COVID-19. No field was left unaffected by it.
 
• Statement C is the second sentence of the passage which explains that education is one of the most severely impacted fields. Millions of youngsters worldwide were unable to receive a quality education.
 
• Statement D is the third sentence of the passage which explains that during the epidemic, millions of teachers who are currently employed—particularly those in private educational institutions were not paid their full salaries.
 
• Statement A is the last sentence of the passage which shows that It is without a doubt clear that this illness caused suffering and anguish in the lives of persons who worked in other professions as well.

Hence, the correct sequence is B, C, D, A

The correct answer is option 2.

The correct passage is: ***B**. Covid-19 changed the form and face of every field in the world. It did not leave any field untouched. **C**. One of the most affected areas is education. Millions of students all over the world could not get a proper education. **D**. Millions of teachers who are working, specifically in private educational institutes, were not paid a full salary during the pandemic. **A**. It is unquestionably evident that this virus brought misery and grief into the lives of people of other professions too.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

Vishnu and family __are looking around into__ the possibility of moving to Canada.
questions.solution:

• Remove the preposition '**around**' to correct the sentence.
 
• Let's look at the meaning of the given phrasal verbs.
 
 
• "**Looking around**" means going through a place in order to see what is there: to explore a place.
 
• "Looking into" means trying to find out about something.
 
• "Looking upto" means to respect and admire someone.
 
 
 
• The sentence is talking about a possibility, so "**looking into**" should be used.
 
• We cannot use two prepositions (around and into) simultaneously in a single sentence. It doesn't make any sense.
 
• The implied meaning of the sentence is: Vishnu and his family are considering relocating to Canada.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**, which can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

**Corrected sentence:** *Vishnu and family are looking into the possibility of moving to Canada.*

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

I remember vivid / the last road trip / we had / before the pandemic hit.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part of the sentence is: **I remember vivid**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Replace the adjective "**vivid**" with the adverb "**vividly**" to correct the sentence.
 
• Adding -**ly **to an adjective makes an adverb.
 
• An **adjective **is a word that describes nouns, such as large or beautiful. 
 
• An **adverb **is a word that describes verbs, adjectives, and other adverbs, such as silently or really.
 
• In the given sentence an adverb should be used because it is describing the verb "remember**.**"
 
• **Vividly **means in a way that produces powerful feelings or strong, clear images in the mind. (एक तरह से जो मन में शक्तिशाली भावनाओं या मजबूत, स्पष्ट छवियों को उत्पन्न करता है)
 
 
• **Example -** *Margaret remembers vividly the day she received the grim news.*
 
 
 
• So, from here we can easily say that using "**vividly**" instead of "vivid" is the correct choice for the given sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4, **which contains an error.

**Corrected sentence:** *I remember **vividly **the last road trip we had before the pandemic hit.*

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.**

Diwali sweets were being prepared by our grandmother.

options.text: Our grandmother was preparing Diwali sweets.
Our grandmother is preparing Diwali sweets.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Our grandmother was preparing Diwali sweets.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The given sentence is in the passive form and we need to change it into the active form.
 
• The given sentence is written in the passive form of the **past continuous tense**.
 
• The past continuous tense in the passive voice has the following structure: **Object+ was/were +being+V3+ by + subject__**
 
• The past continuous tense in the active voice has the following structure: **__Subject + was/were + v1+ing+ object__**
 
• Example - 
 
 
• Passive voice - The wall was being painted by Rahul.
 
• Active voice - Rahul was painting the wall.
 
 
 
• Rules of Conversion from Passive to Active Voice:
 
 
• Identify the subject, the verb, and the object.
 
• Change the object into the subject.
 
• Change the verb into the past participle form of the verb.
 
• Change the subject into an object.
 
 

​Therefore, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct Active Voice: *Our grandmother was preparing Diwali sweets.*

• 'Were' is the second-person singular past and plural past of to be.
